summary: This work distinguishes two populations of correlated errors in superconducting transmon qubits: radiation-induced events with $\tau \approx 5$ ms decay time and pulse-tube (PT)-induced events with longer lifetimes occurring at $\approx 1.4$ Hz. Gap-engineered devices with $\delta\Delta_{JJ} > f_q$ show suppression of both error types, suggesting a quasiparticle-mediated mechanism for PT errors.
motivation: Correlated errors in superconducting qubits degrade quantum error correction performance; understanding their sources enables targeted mitigation. While radiation-induced errors are well-studied, PT vibrations in dilution refrigerators represent an under-characterized and potentially larger source of correlated errors in laboratory-scale systems.
method: Matched filtering with exponential template ($\tau_0 = 5$ ms) was applied to relaxation measurements from 10-qubit arrays in transmon devices. Events were characterized by filter score, decay lifetime, spatial distribution across the qubit array, and frequency content. PT-off measurements, two-DR comparisons, and room-temperature accelerometer measurements (50 kHz sampling) validated the PT-error hypothesis.
result: In DR1, $\approx 99\%$ of detected events were PT-induced; they vanished when the PT was turned off and did not occur in DR2 (which had lower acceleration at PT frequency). Gap-engineered devices ($d_2$: $\delta\Delta_{JJ} \approx 10$ GHz, $d_3$: $\delta\Delta_{JJ} \approx 7$ GHz) showed no detectable radiation or PT-induced events in the same cool-down, while unengineered device $d_1$ ($\delta\Delta_{JJ} < f_q$) exhibited both. PT-off operation increased estimated $T_1$ by $\approx 9$ µs; DR2 showed 2× higher average $T_1$ (76 vs 38 µs) and 2.2× higher $T_2$ (79 vs 36 µs) than DR1.
